question: Which amendment abolished the privy purse and privileges of the former rulers of princely states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Twenty-Sixth Amendment Act, 1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The **Twenty-Sixth Amendment Act, 1971** abolished the **privy purse** and privileges of the former rulers of princely states in India.
 
• The **privy purse** was a payment made to the rulers of princely states as part of their agreement to integrate into the Indian Union after independence.
 
• The amendment removed **Article 291** and **Article 362** of the Indian Constitution, which guaranteed privy purses and privileges to the former rulers.
 
• The abolition was justified on grounds of maintaining equality and ending the feudal system that was inconsistent with the democratic framework of India.
 
• This amendment was introduced by the government of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**, reflecting her commitment to social equity and democratic principles.
